statement: Project points and curves along the UCS Z direction, the current view direction or a two-point vector onto a solid or surface in 3D, optionally trimming the target through SURFACEAUTOTRIM.
superiority: Exact projection result with trims.

acceptance.sketch: Project a circle onto XY plane along Z gives equal circle at Z=0.

notes: Verified against help page "PROJECTGEOMETRY (Command)". Corrected: Targets are solids or surfaces, not planes; no 'normal' direction option is documented. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Project; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row.

statement: Move selected objects from model space to paper space on a layout, or back, rescaling them so they keep the same apparent size and position relative to a chosen layout viewport.
superiority: Annotative-aware transfer.

acceptance.sketch: Object moved from model to paper at viewport scale 1:50 has size 1/50 of model size.

notes: Verified against help page "CHSPACE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers CopyViewportToDetail; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row.

statement: Copy selected objects to the clipboard with a chosen base point so a later paste places them relative to that point.
superiority: Retains attributes and exact placement.

acceptance.sketch: COPYBASE at (0,0) then PASTECLIP at (10,10) shifts by (10,10).

notes: Verified against help page "COPYBASE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Copy; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row.

statement: Paste clipboard objects as a block with a generated name at a chosen insertion point, and paste them at their original coordinates with PASTEORIG, which only works for data from a different drawing.
superiority: Defined name and layer rules.

acceptance.sketch: PASTEBLOCK creates a block with anonymous name A$C...; PASTEORIG keeps coordinates.

notes: Verified against help page "PASTEBLOCK (Command)". Corrected: Row bundles two commands; statement covers both but PASTEORIG should get its own row. Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-7B4B41C4-E9E2-40D5-936F-6BF591E7A2A8 Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Paste; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row.

statement: The program must prompt for new geometry and create an object matching a selected object's type and general properties, copying over type-specific properties like style, scale or name where they apply.

acceptance.sketch: Select a red circle on layer A, run ADDSELECTED and give a new center and radius; a new circle with new geometry is created, also red and on layer A.

notes: Added from help page "ADDSELECTED (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide the command-line legacy ARRAY that creates non-associative 2D rectangular or polar arrays by prompting for rows, columns and spacing or items, angle and center, limited by a maximum element count of 100,000 by default and excluding path arrays and levels.

acceptance.sketch: Run -ARRAY on a circle, choose Rectangular with 3 rows, 4 columns and 10-unit spacing; 12 independent circles result, and a request over the maximum element count is rejected.

notes: Added from help page "-ARRAY (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must create regularly spaced rectangular, path or polar arrays of selected objects, filtering out attributes, with DELOBJ controlling whether the sources are kept.

acceptance.sketch: Run ARRAY on a circle and choose Rectangular, then Polar; the matching ARRAYRECT or ARRAYPOLAR workflow starts and the source objects are kept or deleted per DELOBJ.

notes: Added from help page "ARRAY (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must end the associative-array source-editing state and let the user either keep or discard the edits made to the source objects or replacement items.

acceptance.sketch: Run ARRAYEDIT Source on a 3x3 rectangular array, move the source object, run ARRAYCLOSE and answer No; assert all nine items return to their original geometry, then repeat answering Yes and assert all items reflect the change.

notes: Added from help page "ARRAYCLOSE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide BREAKATPOINT to split an open line, arc, or open polyline into two objects at one specified point, projecting an off-object point onto it, and refuse closed objects such as circles.

acceptance.sketch: Break a line from 0,0 to 10,0 at 4,0; assert two lines 0,0-4,0 and 4,0-10,0 exist; try a circle and assert it is rejected.

notes: Added from help page "BREAKATPOINT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Provide the legacy CHANGE command that edits existing objects, moving the nearest line endpoint, resizing circles, relocating text and blocks, and altering properties such as color, elevation, layer, linetype, linetype scale, lineweight, thickness, transparency, material and annotative.

acceptance.sketch: Select a circle, run CHANGE with a new radius 7, then repeat on a line choosing Properties Layer to a new layer, and assert radius is 7 and the line sits on the new layer.

notes: Added from help page "CHANGE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Provide a command that places selected objects on the system clipboard in every available format so they can be pasted into documents or other drawings, with the richest format used on paste.

acceptance.sketch: Select a circle, run COPYCLIP, paste into another drawing, and assert an identical circle appears.

notes: Added from help page "COPYCLIP (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: CUTBASE must move the selected objects to the Clipboard together with a user-chosen base point and delete them from the drawing, so a later paste is positioned relative to that base point without creating OLE link data.

acceptance.sketch: Select a circle, run CUTBASE with base point at its center; expect the circle erased, and PASTECLIP at a point P places its center at P.

notes: Added from help page "CUTBASE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: CUTCLIP must place the selected objects on the Clipboard while deleting them from the drawing so they can be pasted into this or another drawing or application, without creating OLE link information.

acceptance.sketch: Select a line, run CUTCLIP; expect the line gone and PASTECLIP to restore an identical line.

notes: Added from help page "CUTCLIP (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must provide -HYPERLINK to attach hyperlinks to objects or to a rectangular area (drawn on the URLLAYER layer), each with a target path or URL, optional named location and description, or to remove selected hyperlinks by number, path, or all.

acceptance.sketch: Run -HYPERLINK Insert Object on a circle with URL https://example.com and description 'Spec', assert the link is stored; run Remove with * and assert the circle has no hyperlinks and the removal count is printed.

notes: Added from help page "-HYPERLINK (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must support command-line editing of multiline intersections, breaks and vertices with the cross, tee, corner, add-vertex, delete-vertex, cut-single, cut-all and weld options.

acceptance.sketch: Draw two crossing multilines, run -MLEDIT with CC, pick both, and confirm the crossing is cleaned as a closed cross.

notes: Added from help page "-MLEDIT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must offer, as documented for AutoCAD LT, one command that lets selected objects be moved, copied, rotated and scaled about a chosen base point.

acceptance.sketch: In MOCORO, select a rectangle, set a base point, Move by (5,0), then Scale by 2, and confirm the final position and size.

notes: Added from help page "MOCORO (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: The program must copy objects nested inside an xref, block or DGN underlay directly into the current drawing without exploding or binding the container.

acceptance.sketch: Select a line nested in an xref, run NCOPY with a displacement, and confirm a new line exists in the host drawing and the xref is unchanged.

notes: Added from help page "NCOPY (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: Opening a size and scale dialog for a selected OLE object, OLESCALE must let the user change that object's dimensions, scale and text size, and it requires an OLE object to be selected first.

notes: Added from help page "OLESCALE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: -OVERKILL must delete duplicate and overlapping lines, arcs and polylines and merge partly overlapping or end-to-end ones, with options to ignore chosen properties, set a numeric tolerance, treat polylines as whole objects, and leave associative objects untouched.

notes: Added from help page "-OVERKILL (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

notes: Added from help page "PASTEASHYPERLINK (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

statement: PASTECLIP must paste Clipboard content into the drawing, converting plain text to mtext using MTEXT defaults, spreadsheet data to a table, and other external data to embedded or linked OLE objects, while choosing the richest available format.

notes: Added from help page "PASTEORIG (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

acceptance.sketch: Copy spreadsheet cells, run PASTESPEC, choose a picture format and assert the pasted object is of that type rather than a table.

notes: Added from help page "PASTESPEC (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.

notes: Added from help page "XPLODE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed.
